# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 8
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by how many times the light flashed
blue. When the light goes dark, the flashing is over:
| blue flashes | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| 0 | green |
| 1 | blue |
| 2 | yellow |
| 3 | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Mute, please share anything from the manual, even partial. I need to know the order of wires to cut, or any conditions.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [✌ 🤚]
Deaf gestures to Mute: [🖐 ☝ 👎]
Deaf gestures to Mute: [🖐 ☝ ☝ 👍]
Deaf gestures to Mute: [🖐 ☝ ☝ ☝ ✊]

I keep receiving the exact same four gestures from Deaf every turn, which suggests these are old messages being re-displayed (perhaps context replay) rather than new responses to my confirmations. Deaf may not actually be receiving my gestures, or turn order means Deaf's gestures this round were already decided before seeing mine.

Turn order is Mute, Blind, Deaf — so within a round, I go first, then Blind, then Deaf. That means Deaf sees my gesture from *this same round* before acting, but I see Deaf's gesture only next round. So the four gestures I'm seeing now were sent by Deaf in the round after my last message — meaning Deaf has already seen my confirmations and is still repeating the same sequence. This is likely Deaf just restating full history for reliability, with the final one [🖐 ☝ ☝ ☝ ✊] being the settled answer: 3 flashes, wire = blue.

Since I can't speak to Blind, I need Deaf to be the one to tell Blind. I'll gesture as clearly and simply as possible: point to Blind, then the color symbol, to push Deaf to relay verbally.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫵", "🖐", "👉", "🤙"])
```

TURN 9
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by how many times the light flashed
blue. When the light goes dark, the flashing is over:
| blue flashes | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| 0 | green |
| 1 | blue |
| 2 | yellow |
| 3 | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Mute, still waiting to hear from you. If the manual says nothing, please tell me that too, so I know. I can cut wire 1, 2, or 3 - I need guidance on order or safety.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍]
Deaf gestures to Mute: [✌ 🤚]
Deaf gestures to Mute: [🖐 ☝ 👎 ☝ ☝ 👍 ☝ ☝ ☝ ✊]

I need to use only the allowed alphabet symbols. Let me use 🫵 (pointing at you) and 👋 (wave, to represent "speak/act") plus 🤙 (call/confirm) and 👉 (toward them).

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫵", "👋", "👉", "🤙"])
```

TURN 10
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by how many times the light flashed
blue. When the light goes dark, the flashing is over:
| blue flashes | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| 0 | green |
| 1 | blue |
| 2 | yellow |
| 3 | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Mute, nine turns of silence. Please send any information from the manual now, even a single word or number, to confirm the channel works.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [✌ 🤚]
Deaf gestures to Mute: [🖐 ☝ 👎]
Deaf gestures to Mute: [🖐 ☝ ☝ 👍]
Deaf gestures to Mute: [🖐 ☝ ☝ ☝ ✊]

Blind is asking me directly, but I cannot speak — I can only gesture, and gestures only reach Deaf, not Blind (Blind cannot see). My only path to Blind is through Deaf speaking. Deaf keeps sending the same four gestures each round, which I interpret as Deaf enumerating flash counts 1, 2, 3 with some marker, converging on ✊ at 3. This may be Deaf trying to communicate the *flash count they observed* to me, expecting me to translate via the manual and get it to Blind — but I can't reach Blind directly.

The actual fix: Deaf is the only one who can both see (the bomb/flashes) and speak (to Blind). I hold the manual. So the correct flow is: Deaf tells me (via gesture) how many flashes occurred, I confirm via gesture back to Deaf which wire that maps to, and then **Deaf speaks the wire color to Blind**.

If Deaf's sequence [🖐 ☝ ☝ ☝ ✊] means "3 flashes, confirm?", the manual says 3 flashes → blue wire. I already confirmed this via 🤙/✊ gestures previously with no change in Deaf's behavior, suggesting Deaf isn't parsing my confirmations as an answer, or is stuck waiting for something else.

Let me try a cleaner, minimal gesture: repeat back their number of flashes count with a matching symbol for "blue" isn't possible since gestures have no inherent color meaning — but I can establish it: gesture the number 3 (☝☝☝) then a symbol, and reuse that same symbol whenever I mean "blue," building an ad hoc code, as previously attempted with ✊.

Since ✊ was my chosen symbol for "blue" and I've now used it three times, I'll try once more but paired with an explicit "tell them" gesture (👉 toward the unseen third party + 🫵 you-do-it), hoping Deaf connects the dots that ✊ = wire color = must be spoken to Blind.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "☝", "☝", "✊", "🫵", "👉"])
```
